editionLabel: Schmidt Spiele German rules, article 75046, English summary
firstPlayerRule: Whoever most recently found a gold treasure takes the key card and starts.
officialTieBreak: If nobody has found a gold treasure, the rules offer the youngest player as an alternative starter.
clarifications: The rulebook also says the game ends with everyone losing if nobody has found a gold treasure.
The key-card holder first opens another player's chamber. The owner of that chamber then receives the key.
evidenceNotes: Both the unusual immediate-loss sentence and the youngest-player alternative are explicitly in the source. The latter is not an invented fallback.

editionLabel: Schmidt Spiele German base-game rules, article 49341, English summary
firstPlayerRule: Whoever most recently cooked something is the first round's starting player.
clarifications: That player shuffles the fortune-teller cards, keeps the deck, and reads the opening card aloud.
Players brew their potions simultaneously; the starting-player role does not mean drawing ingredients before everyone else.
evidenceNotes: German starting instruction checked on printed/PDF page 2, round-start card reader on page 3, simultaneous brewing on page 4.
